newsitem.title: USA: First Bank credit card charge-offs up.
newsitem.headline: First Bank credit card charge-offs up.

text.p: First Bank System Inc said Thursday its annualized net credit card charge-offs rose to 3.57 percent of average balances, up from 2.92 percent a year ago and 3.33 percent in the third quarter.
Total annualized loan charge-offs were 0.59 percent of average loans, up from 0.44 percent a year ago, but down from 0.63 percent in the third quarter.
Total net charge-offs were $40.6 million in the quarter, compared with $29.0 million a year ago, the $36.49 billion asset bank holding company said.
But total net charge-offs were down from $42.7 million a year ago.
Consumer loan net charge-offs were $42.8 million, up from $35.7 million, reflecting higher average credit card balances and higher loss ratios, First Bank said.
The bank also said it continues to experience growth in its payment systems and trust businesses.
Trust fees rose to $58.9 million in the quarter from $47.8 million a year ago.

Credit card fees rose to $76.8 million from $61.7 million. But First Bank also said Dayton Hudson Corp's Target Stores has decided to discontinue its cobranded credit card with First Bank to focus on a private label card.
First Bank also said Thursday it bought back four million shares in the fourth quarter under its current repurchase plan.
Earlier Thursday, First Bank reported net income of $171.4 million, or $1.26 a primary share in the fourth quarter, compared to $150.7 million, or $1.14 a share a year ago.
